reviewNotes.provenance: Replayed the complete 5th Sinquefield Cup 2017 game from the checksummed archive, including source ply 46 and previous move Kf8. Verified the master credential and compared the recorded continuation Bxg7+ Kxg7 Qc3+ with the teaching line.

reviews.reason: The pawn closes the mating diagonal, but the vacated f7 square lets White check on a different diagonal and demands a king retreat.
reviews.distinctness: Advance the f-pawn to intercept mate, then answer the diagonal opened by that same pawn move.
reviews.solutionVi: f5 chặn đường chéo e4–h7. Sau Qd5+, Đen đi Kh8 để tránh đường chéo d5–g8. Nếu chắn bằng Rf7, Trắng bắt Xe bằng Nxf7.
hintsVi: Hãy chặn đường Hậu Trắng đến h7. Khi Tốt f7 tiến lên, đường chéo nào mở ra cho Hậu Trắng chiếu?

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: The f5 pawn occupies the queen’s path to h7. Vacating f7 opens the diagonal for Qd5+, so the second move is related to the first.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: Kh8 immediately still permits Qxh7#. Qf5 loses after Qxc6. In the line with f5, Rf7 and Qf7 allow Nxf7.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: Compared Qd5+ and Qc4+, plus all captures after f5. Qxf5 is met by Rxf5. After Kh8, Nxh7 allows Kxh7, while Nb5 and Be3 are the more serious replies.
reviewNotes.level: A pawn block with a direct consequence that the solver must anticipate before the king retreat.
reviewNotes.provenance: Replayed the complete 50th Sitges Open 2026 game (2026.07.25) to source ply 31 and matched the FEN, previous move and game hash. Checked the archive checksum metadata and master evidence. The game follows the teaching line through both solver moves.

reviews.reason: The g-pawn immediately captures the sole mating attacker. Either recapture is an equal pawn exchange and leaves Black’s king safe from immediate mate.
reviews.distinctness: Pawn captures the mating pawn before it can make a supported diagonal capture on g7.
reviews.solutionVi: gxh6 — Tốt đen từ g7 bắt Tốt trắng ở h6. Nước này loại bỏ quân đang dọa chiếu hết. Nếu Đen đi a4, Trắng chiếu hết bằng hxg7#.
hintsVi: Tốt trắng ở h6 đang dọa bắt vào g7 và chiếu hết. Quân đen nào có thể bắt Tốt này ngay?

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: The h6-pawn is the piece that can play hxg7# with the support of the white king on g6. The black pawn captures it from g7.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: Each of the seven other legal roots permits hxg7#, including a4 and the knight moves.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: White has no immediate mate after gxh6. Reviewed both recaptures Kxh6 and gxh6, with Nd6 and Nd4 respectively in bounded continuations. Neither recapture creates a new immediate mate. Ba2 and Kh5 allow hxg5. No offered material.
reviewNotes.level: Eight pieces. A single adjacent pawn capture and a readily visible mate threat.
reviewNotes.provenance: Keymer–Aronian, World Blitz 2025, round 14.12, PGN Mentor Aronian archive. Unmodified FEN after 67.h6. Black played 67...gxh6.

reviews.reason: Kb4 alone gets the king out of the knight’s mating net and creates several safe king moves against the intended check.
reviews.distinctness: Direct king relocation against a knight check. The king still gets checked on b4, but it can now reach the c-file.
reviews.solutionVi: Mã đen dọa Nc6#. Trắng đi Kb4 — Vua từ a5 đến b4. Nếu Đen đi Nc6+, Vua trắng có thể sang c5.
hintsVi: Khi Mã đen đến c6, Vua trắng cần đứng ở đâu để có thể chạy sang c5?

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: After Ne5, the threat Nc6# catches the king on a5. Moving to b4 makes c5 and four other safe squares reachable against Nc6+.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: Independent replay of all 12 legal moves. Each of the 11 alternatives allows Nc6#.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: Checked all 16 legal Black replies after Kb4. Nc6+ Kc5, Nd3+ Kc3 and a5+ Kc5 handle all three checks. Quiet Kc6 f6 and Kc8 Kc5 are the strongest analyzed continuations. None of the replies renews an immediate mate threat and no piece is offered by Kb4.
reviewNotes.level: Ten pieces, two of them minor pieces. The corner-side knight threat and the king escape are visible in one move.
reviewNotes.provenance: Replayed the 101-ply Julius Baer Play-In PGN Mentor game from the initial position. Malakhov played 43...Ne5, and Meier played 44.Kb4.

reviews.reason: Nxd5 removes the mating queen and she cannot be recaptured.
reviews.distinctness: Direct removal of a queen by the knight, with a natural b-pawn push as the false lead.
reviews.solutionVi: Nxd5 — Mã trắng từ f6 đến d5 bắt Hậu đen. Khi Hậu rời bàn cờ, đòn chiếu hết Qd1# không còn. Nếu Trắng đẩy Tốt lên b5 trước, Đen chiếu hết bằng Qd1#.
hintsVi: Hậu đen có thể xuống d1 để chiếu hết. Quân trắng nào bắt được Hậu ngay?

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: A legal null-move threat probe identifies Qd1#. Nxd5 removes the mating queen and she cannot be recaptured.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: Independent exhaustive replay found immediate mate after all 12 alternative legal starts.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: Seven Black replies, with no checking or capturing reply. Ke6, Ke8, Kf8 and e4 are in the engine evidence. The knight cannot be recaptured, and the remaining black pawn g3 does not deliver immediate mate.
reviewNotes.level: 9 pieces after the answer. Reviewed as a one-decision position with no defining material offer.
reviewNotes.provenance: Complete replay matches the unmodified FEN and preceding move. Matyassy,Lazar–Yurovskykh,Oleksandr, 2nd 3-0 Thu 9th Jul 2026, 2026.07.09. Nxd5 was played. Archive https://theweekinchess.com/zips/twic1653g.zip.

reviews.reason: Ka3 protects the knight on a4. The very capture that would have delivered mate now lets the king recapture the rook.
reviews.distinctness: A four-piece position in which the threatened mate is a capture of the solver’s own knight. The defence protects that knight and the king at the same time.
reviews.solutionVi: Ka3 — Vua trắng từ a2 đến a3, bảo vệ Mã ở a4. Nếu Đen bắt Mã và chiếu bằng Rxa4+, Vua trắng bắt lại Xe bằng Kxa4. Nếu Vua trắng đi a1, Đen chiếu hết bằng Rxa4#.
hintsVi: Xe đen dọa bắt Mã ở a4 và chiếu hết. Vua trắng có thể đến ô nào để bảo vệ Mã?

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: The black rook attacks the knight on a4. Ka3 places the king next to its own knight, so Rxa4+ permits Kxa4.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: There are exactly two legal starting moves. Ka1 allows Rxa4#.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: After Ka3, Rxa4+ is Black’s sole check and capture and is met by Kxa4. Reviewed strongest bounded Rb8 Nc5, Kd3 Kb4, and the played Ra7 Kb4. No sacrifice or renewed mating threat.
reviewNotes.level: Four pieces and only two choices. Defending the knight makes the tactical idea immediately visible.
reviewNotes.provenance: Herrera Jimenez–Janaszak, 2nd 3-0 Thu 14th May 2026 round 10, The Week in Chess 1645. Unmodified FEN after 57...Ra8. 58.Ka3 was played. Rxa4+ Kxa4 is analysis.

reviews.reason: Kh4 opens the diagonal escape to g3 against Rh8+, with no further preparation.
reviews.distinctness: The king moves along the board edge to gain a diagonal escape from a single rook. The white pawns help seal off other king routes.
reviews.solutionVi: Kh4 — Vua đen từ h5 đến h4. Nếu Trắng chiếu Rh8+, Vua đen thoát qua g3. Nếu Vua đen đi h6, Trắng chiếu hết bằng Rh8#.
hintsVi: Xe trắng đang dọa chiếu hết ở h8. Hãy so sánh h4 và h6 để tìm ô cho Vua đen đường thoát sang g3.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: After Kh4 the same rook check on h8 allows Kg3.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All 12 other legal roots allow Rh8#, including the other king move Kh6 and the tempting passed-pawn advance d3.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: After Kh4, White has no immediate mate. Checked Rh8+ Kg3, the strong Ke5 Rf2 and Ke6 Re2+ lines, plus Rxc3 dxc3. No offered material.
reviewNotes.level: Eight pieces. One king move and a visible escape square. No material calculation is needed to find the defense.
reviewNotes.provenance: Andreikin–Artemiev, Titled Tuesday 8 September 2026 round 6, The Week in Chess 1662. Unmodified FEN after 47.f3. 47...Kh4 was played. Rh8+ Kg3 is analysis.

reviews.reason: Bxe4 takes the attacking rook and stops Re8#.
reviews.distinctness: A bishop immediately recaptures the rook that created the mate threat on the preceding move.
reviews.solutionVi: Trắng dọa Re8#. Đen đi Bxe4 — Tượng từ f3 đến e4, bắt Xe trắng đang dọa chiếu hết. Nếu Trắng chiếu g7+, Vua đen có thể thoát sang h7.
hintsVi: Quân đen nào có thể bắt Xe trắng đang chuẩn bị lên e8?

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: The rook on e4 threatens Re8#, with the g6 and h6 pawns covering the escape squares. Bxe4 takes that rook.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: Independent enumeration found Re8# after each of the seven alternatives, including Kg8 and the non-capturing bishop moves.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: The only forcing reply g7+ allows Kh7. Against Kg5 and Kh5 the bishop can capture on g6. The strongest lines settle near equality and the remaining pawns do not refute the defence.
reviewNotes.level: Six pieces. One bishop recapture removes the mating piece. No sacrifice or complicated preparation.
reviewNotes.provenance: Complete Mamedyarov–Vogel game, Austrian Team Championship 2023–24, 21 March 2024, Mamedyarov archive. The original position follows 77.Rxe4. The game continued 77...Bxe4 78.Kg5 Bxg6.

reviews.reason: g5 is the only move that frees a flight square against the immediate knight mate.
reviews.distinctness: A quiet pawn move frees a square for the king while a knight threatens mate.
reviews.solutionVi: Đen dọa Nf4#. Trắng đi g5 — Tốt từ g4 đến g5, nhường ô g4 cho Vua. Sau Nf4+, Trắng thoát chiếu bằng Kg4. Nếu Đen bắt Tốt bằng hxg5, Trắng có thể dùng Tốt h4 bắt lại.
hintsVi: Tốt trắng nào đang chiếm ô thoát của Vua khi Mã đen nhảy đến f4?

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Black threatens Nf4#. The white g4-pawn occupies the king’s safe escape square, and g5 clears it.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: Independent exhaustive legal replay found Nf4# after all nine alternatives, each a bishop move.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: Nf4+ allows Kg4. After hxg5, hxg5 or Kxg5 restores the pawn exchange. Nxh4 allows gxh6+ Kh7 Kxh4. Other strong quiet replies Kh7 and Ne1 allow Be8 and Bc6 respectively.
reviewNotes.level: Nine pieces and one pawn move. The possible pawn capture allows an immediate recapture, and the king’s escape is visible.
reviewNotes.provenance: Complete Karpov–Bacrot game, Cap d’Agde 2006, Karpov archive. Original position follows 65...Ng2, and 66.g5 was played.

reviews.reason: Kh2 alone allows the king to capture a rook that checks from h1.
reviews.distinctness: The king defends the mating square directly and can take the checking rook.
reviews.solutionVi: Đen dọa Rh1#. Trắng đi Kh2 — Vua từ h3 đến h2. Nếu Xe đen vẫn chiếu Rh1+, Vua trắng bắt Xe bằng Kxh1.
hintsVi: Vua trắng cần đứng ở ô nào để có thể bắt Xe đen nếu Xe xuống h1?

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Black threatens Rh1#. Kh2 places the white king next to h1 and the black king on f3 does not protect that square.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: Independent exhaustive legal replay found Rh1# after all eight alternatives, including g4 and all rook moves.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: Rh1+ allows Kxh1. Against Ra2+, Kh3 escapes and White keeps an active rook after Kf2 Rh8. Rxa7 is met by Rxa7. The stronger quiet e4 and Ke3 allow Rf8 and g4 respectively.
reviewNotes.level: Ten pieces and one king move with a direct capture of the potential mating piece. No sacrifice.
reviewNotes.provenance: Complete Piket–Karpov game, Amber Rapid, Monte Carlo 1993, Karpov archive. Original position follows 59...Ra1, and 60.Kh2 was played.

reviews.reason: Kxa2 removes the pawn before it can capture on b1 and promote with mate.
reviews.distinctness: The defender captures an advanced pawn to prevent a capture-promotion mate, with only one other move to compare.
reviews.solutionVi: Đen dọa dùng Tốt a2 bắt Tượng ở b1 và phong Hậu chiếu hết bằng axb1=Q#. Trắng đi Kxa2 — Vua từ a1 đến a2, bắt Tốt. Nếu Đen bắt Tượng bằng Rxb1, Trắng bắt lại Xe bằng Kxb1.
hintsVi: Quân đen nào có thể bắt Tượng ở b1 rồi phong cấp ngay?

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: The black rook pins the bishop against the king on a1 and would protect the new queen on b1. Kxa2 removes the source of the promotion threat.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: Independent enumeration found two legal moves. Kb2 permits axb1=Q#, while Kxa2 leaves no immediate mate.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: Rg2+ allows Ka1, with the bishop available to meet a further rank-one check. Rxb1 allows Kxb1, leaving only the kings. Strong quiet replies include Kc3 Bf5 and Rg5 Kb2 in the bounded evidence.
reviewNotes.level: Five pieces. One king capture. The pinned bishop and the pawn one rank from promotion are visible. No sacrifice.
reviewNotes.provenance: Complete Kosteniuk–Bacrot game, Titled Tuesday early, 19 April 2022, Bacrot archive. The original position follows 119...a2, and 120.Kxa2 was played.

reviews.reason: Ba7 guards the promotion square. The bishop captures on b8 if the pawn promotes to a queen or a rook with check.
reviews.distinctness: A bishop stops two promotion mates by controlling the square of promotion rather than taking the attacking pawn.
reviews.solutionVi: Ba7 — Tượng đen từ c5 đến a7, bảo vệ ô b8. Nếu Tốt trắng phong Hậu hoặc Xe và chiếu ở b8, Tượng đen bắt quân vừa phong bằng Bxb8.
hintsVi: Tốt trắng ở b7 dọa phong Hậu hoặc Xe và chiếu hết. Tượng đen đi đâu để có thể bắt quân vừa phong ở b8?

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: The pawn on b7 can mate by promoting to either queen or rook on b8. Ba7 enables Bxb8 in both cases.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All ten other legal starts allow both b8=Q# and b8=R#, including Ke8 and Bb6.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: Both forcing promotions b8=Q+ and b8=R+ are met by Bxb8. The bishop promotion can also be captured, and knight promotion gives no check. Reviewed quiet bishop moves met by Bb8, and the played Kb5. No sacrifice or renewed mate threat.
reviewNotes.level: Ten pieces. The single diagonal move answers a direct, visible promotion threat.
reviewNotes.provenance: Bendayan Claros–Quispe Arteaga, Titled Tuesday 23 June 2026 round 1, The Week in Chess 1651. Unmodified FEN after 48.b7. 48...Ba7 was played. The promotion examples are analysis.

reviews.reason: Ka5 immediately makes b6 reachable against Ra1+, with no materially costly offer.
reviews.distinctness: In the rook mating net, the solver chooses between two legal moves along the a-file. The pawn on c4 and rook on c5 shape a distinct upper escape.
reviews.solutionVi: Ka5 — Vua trắng từ a4 đến a5. Trong ván đấu, Đen chiếu Ra1+ và Vua trắng thoát sang b6 bằng Kb6. Nếu Vua đi Ka3, Đen chiếu hết bằng Ra1#.
hintsVi: Khi Xe đen lên a1, từ a3 hay a5 Vua trắng có thể chạy sang b6?

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: A legal null-move threat probe identifies Ra1#. Ka5 immediately makes b6 reachable against Ra1+, with no materially costly offer.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: Independent exhaustive replay found immediate mate after all 7 alternative legal starts.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: Ra1+ Kb6 is played. Rb5+ is met by a safe reply, and the strong quiet Kd4 does not immediately rebuild Ra1#. All 20 opposing replies checked for renewed threats.
reviewNotes.level: 7 pieces after the answer. Reviewed as a one-decision position with no defining material offer.
reviewNotes.provenance: Complete replay matches the unmodified FEN and preceding move. Khayrullin,D–Mahdian,Anousha, 12th Cesme Open A 2026, 2026.06.30. Ka5 was played. Archive https://theweekinchess.com/zips/twic1652g.zip.

reviews.reason: Kf5 moves the king away from the knight’s mating net and opens several flight squares after Ne3+.
reviews.distinctness: Only a king move works against a knight mate. The pawn push e3 looks like it blocks the knight’s destination, but the knight simply captures on that square with mate.
reviews.solutionVi: Kf5 — Vua đen từ g4 đến f5. Trong ván đấu, Trắng chiếu Ne3+ và Vua đen thoát qua e6. Nếu Đen đẩy Tốt lên e3 ngay, Trắng bắt Tốt và chiếu hết bằng Nxe3#.
hintsVi: Mã trắng ở d1 đang dọa chiếu hết tại e3. Vua đen có thể đi đâu để còn đường thoát sau khi Mã chiếu?

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Ne3# depends on the black king having no legal escape from g4. Kf5 changes that geometry. The played Ne3+ allows Ke6.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All four alternatives allow immediate mate. The moves a2, g5 and g6 allow Ne3#, and e3 allows Nxe3#.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: White has no mate after Kf5. Both checks were tested: Ne3+ allows Kg6, Kf6, Ke6 and Ke5, and g4+ can be answered by Kxg4. Bounded quiet replies Nc3 and Kf2 leave viable play. No material offer.
reviewNotes.level: Nine pieces, five legal moves. One direct king step solves the problem, with a clear refutation of the pawn alternative.
reviewNotes.provenance: Giri–So, chess.com Speed 2017 round 1.18, PGN Mentor Giri archive. Unmodified FEN after 45.Nd1. 45...Kf5 46.Ne3+ Ke6 was played.

reviews.reason: f4 vacates f3 so that the king can retreat from the mating pawn check.
reviews.distinctness: A pawn creates a flight square against an enemy pawn check while remaining recoverable by immediate equal exchange.
reviews.solutionVi: f4 — Tốt trắng từ f3 đến f4, nhường ô f3 cho Vua. Trong ván đấu, Đen chiếu h5+ và Trắng thoát bằng Kf3. Nếu Đen bắt Tốt bằng exf4, Trắng có thể bắt lại bằng gxf4.
hintsVi: Nếu Đen đẩy Tốt lên h5 để chiếu, quân trắng nào đang đứng trên ô thoát f3?

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: A legal null-move threat probe identifies h5#. f4 vacates f3 so that the king can retreat from the mating pawn check.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: Independent exhaustive replay found immediate mate after all 11 alternative legal starts.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: The strongest h5+ gives Kf3. If exf4, gxf4 or Kxf4 immediately recovers equal material. Rh4+ gxh4 and f5+ exf5+ are legal and do not leave immediate mate.
reviewNotes.level: 10 pieces after the answer. Reviewed as a one-decision position with no defining material offer.
reviewNotes.provenance: Complete replay matches the unmodified FEN and preceding move. Fedosov,Alexander–Laddha,Shubh Jayesh, Titled Tue 19th May 2026, 2026.05.19. f4 was played. Archive https://theweekinchess.com/zips/twic1646g.zip.

reviews.reason: Nd3 cuts the bishop’s line to e2, so the king can capture the rook if it checks there. The knight can be recaptured in an even exchange.
reviews.distinctness: A knight interposes between a supporting bishop and the mating square, allowing the king to take the checking rook.
reviews.solutionVi: Nd3 — Mã trắng từ c5 đến d3, chặn đường Tượng đen bảo vệ e2. Nếu Đen chiếu Re2+, Vua trắng bắt Xe bằng Kxe2. Nếu Đen đổi Tượng lấy Mã bằng Bxd3, Trắng bắt lại bằng Kxd3.
hintsVi: Tượng đen ở c4 bảo vệ ô e2 qua d3. Quân trắng nào có thể chắn đường chéo đó?

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Black’s Re2# relies on the bishop on c4 guarding e2 through d3. Nd3 blocks that line, so Re2+ is met by Kxe2.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All 15 other legal roots, including the active capture Rxf6 and b5, allow Re2#.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: Checked every immediate mate after Nd3. Re2+ Kxe2, Rxb4 Rxb4 and Bxd3 Kxd3 were verified. The last is an even minor-piece exchange. The strong rook moves Rb3 and Ra2 switch to different play, with bounded lines near equality and no renewed mate. No sacrifice.
reviewNotes.level: Ten pieces. The single interposition has a visible line and a direct king capture.
reviewNotes.provenance: Duda–Ponomariov, World Blitz 2015, Berlin round 14.24, PGN Mentor Ponomariov archive. Unmodified FEN after 63...Kg4. 64.Nd3 was played. Re2+ Kxe2 is analysis.

reviews.reason: Kf8 immediately opens inward escape squares against the supported Qg7 check.
reviews.distinctness: A queen protected by its king threatens mate next to the defending king. The defender steps along the back rank so that the same check allows an escape toward the centre.
reviews.solutionVi: Kf8 — Vua đen từ g8 đến f8. Trong phương án phân tích, nếu Trắng chiếu Qg7+, Vua đen có thể thoát qua e8. Nếu Đen bắt Tốt bằng Rxa6, Trắng chiếu hết bằng Qg7#.
hintsVi: Hậu trắng dọa chiếu hết ở g7 với sự hỗ trợ của Vua trắng. Vua đen có thể đi đâu để mở đường thoát về e8?

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: White threatens Qg7# supported by Kh6. Kf8 makes Ke8 and Ke7 legal after Qg7+.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All 13 other legal roots allow Qg7#, including the material capture Rxa6. Rd8 also allows Qxd8#.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: White has no immediate mate after Kf8. All checks and captures reviewed. The main continuations Qg7+ Ke8, Qd6+ Ke8 and Qh8+ Ke7 leave escape paths. Qd8+ is met by Rxd8, Qxf7+ by Kxf7, Qe7+ by Kxe7, and Qxg6 by fxg6. The strongest bounded lines feature continuing checks without a verified forced mate. No material offer.
reviewNotes.level: Ten pieces. One visible escape against the named threat. The lesson makes no claim about the eventual result.
reviewNotes.provenance: Vaganian–Shanava, 15th Ordix Open, Mainz 2008 round 9, PGN Mentor Vaganian archive. Unmodified FEN after 58.Kh6, the final recorded move. 58...Kf8 is verified analysis.

reviews.reason: Kh2 directly leaves the bishop’s mating diagonal and makes the intended king move to g3 illegal.
reviews.distinctness: Discovered bishop mate triggered by a king move. The defence leaves a diagonal instead of preparing to capture a checking rook.
reviews.solutionVi: Vua đen dọa Kg3#: khi Vua rời f3, Tượng e4 sẽ chiếu Vua trắng theo đường chéo e4–h1. Trắng đi Kh2 — Vua từ h1 đến h2, rời đường chéo đó và khống chế ô g3.
hintsVi: Quan sát đường chéo từ Tượng e4 đến Vua trắng. Vua trắng có thể rời đường chéo đó bằng nước nào?

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Kg3# moves the black king out of the e4–h1 bishop diagonal and covers the h2 escape. Kh2 both steps out of that diagonal and prevents the black king from legally moving next to it on g3.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: Replayed all seven legal roots. Each of the six alternatives permits Kg3#, including the bishop moves and f5.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: Checked all 17 Black replies. Bg3+ is a different check, with Kg1 the only move preventing immediate mate after it. Bg1+ allows Kxg1 and Kh3. The strongest quiet Bh4 allows Kg1. After Bxe3, Bxe3 Kxe3 is an equal exchange of bishops after Black takes the attacked pawn. The root offers no piece and none of Black's replies renews an immediate mate threat outside the legal checks.
reviewNotes.level: Seven pieces. The discovered check and diagonal exit are one visible decision. The checking continuations require ordinary king evasion and the original Kg3 mate is gone.
reviewNotes.provenance: Replayed all 195 plies of Klukin–Bok in TWIC 1651. Black played 95...Bf2 and White played 96.Kh2. The recorded continuation starts Bg3+ Kg1.

reviews.reason: Ra7 alone pins the pawn that threatens mate. It directly removes the threat and creates no material offer.
reviews.distinctness: Absolute pin of the mating pawn. This is closely analogous to the color-reversed e77ec191aa2aae9a, so prefer one for final coverage. Here Rxe5 is an attractive false capture and the original game has no repetition claim at the starting position.
reviews.solutionVi: Đen dọa g6#. Trắng đi Ra7 — Xe từ a5 đến a7. Xe trắng ghim Tốt g7 vào Vua đen ở h7. Tốt đen không thể đi g6 vì sẽ để Vua bị chiếu.
hintsVi: Tìm hàng ngang có cả Vua đen và Tốt đang dọa chiếu hết.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: g6# is pending. Only Ra7 lines up the rook with the g7 pawn and the king on h7, so moving the pawn would leave the king in check.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: Replayed all 11 legal roots. The other ten permit g6#, including Ra8, Ra6 and the capture Rxe5.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: All 15 Black replies were checked. The only check, Rg5+, is met by hxg5, and fxg5 can then be met by Kxg5. The strongest quiet Rc2 and Re2 allow Rd7 and Rc7 respectively. Kg8 unpins the pawn by leaving the rank but allows Ra8+ and creates no renewed immediate mate. Ra7 offers no material.
reviewNotes.level: Nine pieces, with a visible absolute pin and no preparatory or sacrificial move.
reviewNotes.provenance: Replayed all 163 plies of Mason–Lasker, Hastings 1895, from the PGN Mentor Lasker archive. Lasker played 60...Kh7, then Mason played 61.Ra7. The recorded reply was Re2.

reviews.reason: Kh7 uniquely guards the mating square. Each of the four tempting g1 promotions permits mate.
reviews.distinctness: Useful reserve with two visible plans in conflict. The defender must protect h8 even with a pawn ready to promote, and the other legal king step also loses.
reviews.solutionVi: Trắng dọa Rh8#. Đen đi Kh7 — Vua từ h6 đến h7. Sau Rh8+, Vua đen bắt Xe bằng Kxh8. Nếu Đen phong Hậu ngay bằng g1=Q, Trắng chiếu hết bằng Rh8#.
hintsVi: Tốt đen ở g2 chỉ còn một ô nữa là phong cấp. Trước khi đẩy Tốt, hãy tìm đòn chiếu hết mà Trắng đang dọa.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: White threatens Rh8# from d8. Kh7 covers the checking square. Kh5 cannot reach h8, and the white king and h3-pawn control the g-file escape squares.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: Independent enumeration found Rh8# after all 17 alternatives, including Kh5 and each promotion on g1.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: Rh8+ allows Kxh8. The strongest Rd7+ allows Kh6 in analysis and continued play. Quiet replies leave Black substantial advantage in the bounded screen. No relevant capture offer after Kh7.
reviewNotes.level: Ten pieces and one direct king move. The near-promotion pawn is a visible distraction and the threat is resolved by the first move.
reviewNotes.provenance: Complete Kempinski–Van Wely game, European Team Championship, Gothenburg, 7 August 2005, Van Wely archive. Original FEN follows 48.Rd8. The game recorded 48...Kh7 49.Rd7+ and a draw. Kxh8 and the escape after Rd7+ are analysis.

reviews.reason: Kc1 uniquely covers d1 while also attacking the black rook on its starting square d2.
reviews.distinctness: The king moves sideways toward the short rook check on d1 and can also take the rook on d2 if Black ignores the attack.
reviews.solutionVi: Đen dọa Rd1#. Trắng đi Kc1 — Vua từ b1 đến c1. Sau Rd1+, Vua trắng bắt Xe bằng Kxd1. Từ c1, Vua trắng cũng tấn công Xe đang đứng ở d2.
hintsVi: Vua trắng cần đứng ở đâu để bắt được Xe đen nếu Xe xuống d1?

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: The rook on d2 threatens Rd1# and the black king on b3 covers White’s second-rank escapes. Kc1 places the white king next to both d1 and d2.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: Independent enumeration found Rd1# after all six alternatives, including Ka1, the free-looking Bxg7 and the passed-pawn advance d7.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: Rd1+ allows Kxd1, Rc2+ allows Kd1, Rxd6 allows Bxd6, and Kxa3 allows Kxd2. The strongest quiet rook moves Rd5, Rd3 and Rd4 give Black playable pressure without a mating refutation.
reviewNotes.level: Nine pieces and one direct king move. The black rook is one step from its mating square and no sacrifice is needed.
reviewNotes.provenance: Complete Saemisch–Spielmann game, Berlin 1926, Spielmann archive. Original FEN follows 79...Kb3. The game played 80.Kc1 Rd4 81.Be7. Rd1+ Kxd1 is analysis.

reviews.reason: Re6 uniquely pins the mating knight to the black king and prevents both knight mates.
reviews.distinctness: A quiet rook move defends by pinning the attacking piece. The apparently forcing Rd3+ fails to a knight capture that mates.
reviews.solutionVi: Đen dọa Nf3#. Trắng đi Re6 — Xe từ d6 đến e6, ghim Mã e5 vào Vua đen ở e3. Mã không thể đi f3 vì sẽ để Vua đen bị chiếu. Nếu Trắng thử Rd3+, Đen bắt Xe và chiếu hết bằng Nxd3#.
hintsVi: Xe trắng có thể đứng ở đâu để ngăn Mã e5 rời cột e?

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Nf3# is the immediate threat. Re6 pins Ne5 against Ke3. After the pin the knight cannot legally move to f3 or d3, and Black has no checking or capturing reply.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: Independent enumeration found Nf3#, Nd3# or Nxd3# after each of the 15 alternatives. Rd3+ allows Nxd3# and moving the rook off the d-file on rank six often gives Black both Nf3# and Nd3#.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: Every reply is quiet. The two strongest king moves Kd4 and Kf4 allow Kxe2. After c3, Rxe5+ wins the pinned knight. Kd3 allows Rxe5. No material is offered.
reviewNotes.level: Nine pieces and one direct rook move. The rook, knight and king are aligned on one file, so the pin can be seen immediately.
reviewNotes.provenance: Complete Larsen–Bronstein game, Moscow 1962, Bronstein archive. Original FEN follows 56...Ke3. The game played 57.Re6 Kd4 58.h6. Rd3+ Nxd3# and the listed replies to Re6 are analysis except for the recorded moves.

reviews.reason: Ne5+ dislodges the white king from g6. Each of its four legal escapes changes the knight mating net.
reviews.distinctness: Knight countercheck clears a king escape against a knight mate. Only six pieces.
reviews.solutionVi: Ne5+ — Mã đen từ g4 đến e5 chiếu Vua. Trong ván đấu, Trắng đáp Kf6. Vua trắng rời g6, nên nếu Mã trắng chiếu Ne7+, Vua đen đã có ô h7 để thoát. Nếu Đen đẩy Tốt lên a4 ngay, Trắng chiếu hết bằng Ne7#.
hintsVi: Ô nào cho phép Mã đen chiếu và buộc Vua trắng rời g6?

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: A legal null-move threat probe identifies Ne7#. Ne5+ dislodges the white king from g6. Each of its four legal escapes changes the knight mating net.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: Independent exhaustive replay found immediate mate after all 6 alternative legal starts.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: Against Kf6 the original Ne7 motif gives the black king h7. Kg5, Kh6 and Kh5 also disperse the net. Exact enumeration finds no renewed mate in one after any of these four replies. No offer.
reviewNotes.level: 6 pieces after the answer. Reviewed as a one-decision position with no defining material offer.
reviewNotes.provenance: Complete replay matches the unmodified FEN and preceding move. Jobava,Ba–Vidit,S, MrDodgy Invitational 2, 2021.05.15. Ne5+ was played. Archive https://www.pgnmentor.com/players/Jobava.zip.

reviews.reason: The rook check forces the enemy king off g5 or a rook block White can capture with check. The strongest reply Kxf6 gives the white king g4 and removes the original mating net.
reviews.distinctness: A countercheck displaces the opposing king from its guard of g4. Compare the rejected Short example, where the threat remains after the opponent answers the check.
reviews.solutionVi: Rc5+ — Xe trắng từ c7 đến c5, chiếu Vua. Trong ván đấu, Đen đáp Kxf6. Vua đen rời g5 nên Vua trắng có ô g4 để thoát. Nếu Trắng đẩy Tốt lên g4 ngay, Đen chiếu hết bằng Rf3#.
hintsVi: Đen đang dọa Rh2#. Vua đen ở g5 khống chế ô thoát g4. Xe trắng có thể chiếu Vua từ ô nào?

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: The mating attack depends on the black king guarding g4. After Rc5+ Kxf6 the king no longer guards it and there is no immediate mate against a pass.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All 23 other legal starts allow mate in one. Most allow Rh2#, and the tempting g4 allows Rf3#.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: All Black replies reviewed: Kxf6 Kg4, Rd5 Rxd5+ and Rf5 Rxf5#. The f6-pawn was already en prise to the king before the check. Rc5+ creates no material offer.
reviewNotes.level: Ten pieces. The direct decision is to check the king that guards the flight square. The main illustration shows the resulting escape and does not require selecting a second defensive maneuver to remove the threat.
reviewNotes.provenance: Kramnik–Klekowski, Titled Tuesday Early 4 July 2023 round 3, PGN Mentor Kramnik archive. Unmodified FEN after 53...Rdd2. 54.Rc5+ Kxf6 55.Kg4 was played.

reviews.reason: Rf4+ removes the supporting king from f6. Neither original queen mate survives any of White’s three legal replies.
reviews.distinctness: A rook countercheck breaks a king-and-queen mating net with two simultaneous threats. The displaced king had been guarding the two mating squares themselves.
reviews.solutionVi: Rf4+ — Xe đen từ e4 đến f4, chiếu Vua. Trong ván đấu, Trắng đáp Ke5. Vua trắng rời f6 nên Hậu mất chỗ dựa ở g5 và g6. Nếu Đen đi h3 ngay, Trắng chiếu hết bằng Qg5#.
hintsVi: Vua trắng ở f6 hỗ trợ cả Qg5# và Qg6#. Xe đen có thể chiếu từ ô nào để buộc Vua trắng rời f6?

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: White threatens Qg5# and Qg6#, each supported by Kf6. All three legal replies to Rf4+ remove the white king from f6. Ke5 and Ke7 leave both g5 and g6 undefended by the king, and Kg7 blocks the queen’s route to them.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: Each of the 18 other legal moves allows an immediate mate. Kh6 allows Qh8# or Qg6#, and h3 allows Qg5#.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: Exhausted the three White replies Ke5, Ke7, and Kg7. None leaves any immediate mate threat against a pass, confirming that the check changes the position permanently. Checked the bounded Ke5 Rf5+ and Ke7 h3 continuations and the less strong Kg7. Rf4+ offers no material.
reviewNotes.level: Seven pieces. One rook move removes the support for both mating checks, with no follow-up defence required to stop them.
reviewNotes.provenance: Pranesh–Niemann, Quantbox Chennai GM 2026 round 5.1, The Week in Chess 1654. Unmodified FEN after 76.Kf6. 76...Rf4+ 77.Ke5 was played.

reviews.reason: exf6 removes the pawn guarding g7 and opens the e-file for the defending rook at the same time.
reviews.distinctness: A pawn capture neutralizes two distinct queen mates by changing both a defended square and a rook line.
reviews.solutionVi: exf6 — Tốt đen từ e7 đến f6 bắt Tốt trắng. Nếu Hậu trắng chiếu Qe8+, Xe đen bắt Hậu bằng Rxe8. Nếu Hậu chiếu Qg7+, Vua đen bắt Hậu bằng Kxg7 vì Tốt trắng ở f6 đã bị bắt.
hintsVi: Đen cần vừa mở đường cho Xe lên e8, vừa bỏ quân đang bảo vệ ô g7. Tốt đen ở e7 có thể làm cả hai việc bằng cách nào?

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: A legal null-move threat probe identifies Qe8#, Qg7#. exf6 removes the pawn guarding g7 and opens the e-file for the defending rook at the same time.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: Independent exhaustive replay found immediate mate after all 17 alternative legal starts.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: Qe8+ Rxe8 and Qg7+ Kxg7 verify both geometric changes. The game’s Qxf6+ Kg8 removes a pawn but not by sacrifice: the white pawn on f6 was captured first. Other checked replies do not renew either mate.
reviewNotes.level: 8 pieces after the answer. Reviewed as a one-decision position with no defining material offer.
reviewNotes.provenance: Complete replay matches the unmodified FEN and preceding move. Jobava,Ba–Artemiev,V, Titled Tuesday 27th Oct, 2020.10.27. exf6 was played. Archive https://www.pgnmentor.com/players/Jobava.zip.

reviews.reason: Bxb1 alone captures the new queen before it can mate along either diagonal.
reviews.distinctness: Immediate capture of a newly promoted queen that has two mating routes. Existing active Bxe4 also captures the attacker, but there is one rook route there and no promotion decision.
reviews.solutionVi: Đen vừa phong Hậu ở b1 và dọa Qb2# hoặc Qa1#. Trắng đi Bxb1 — Tượng từ a2 đến b1, bắt Hậu và hóa giải cả hai đe dọa.
hintsVi: Hậu đen vừa được phong ở b1. Quân trắng nào có thể bắt Hậu ngay?

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Black threatens Qb2# and Qa1# after b1=Q. Either check strikes along a diagonal toward h8. Bxb1 takes away both mating routes.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: Independently replayed all seven legal White moves. The six alternatives all allow both Qb2# and Qa1#.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: Checked all three replies Kf7, Ke8 and Ke7. The queen capture cannot be recaptured and the black king has no renewed immediate mate. The strongest Kf7 can be met by the played Ba2+ or the reviewed Bd3. After Ke8 and Ke7, Kg8 is available. The promotion conversion is outside the immediate defensive objective.
reviewNotes.level: Five pieces. The sole capture removes the attacker and requires no preparation or material offer.
reviewNotes.provenance: Replayed all 129 plies of Reprintsev–Castro Lombana from TWIC 1668. Black played 62...b1=Q and White played 63.Bxb1, with 63...Kf7 as the recorded reply.

reviews.reason: Kg3 immediately moves the white king out of the mating net. The knight check on f5 then has several evasion squares.
reviews.distinctness: This is the six-piece version of the h4 knight-mate net also seen in the fresh Marin Ferragut–Villa Tornero candidate. The active Meier–Malakhov example instead uses an a-file cage and a different flight against Nc6#. This example isolates the role of the pawn that controls g4.
reviews.solutionVi: Kg3 — Vua trắng từ h4 đến g3. Nếu Đen chiếu Nf5+, Vua trắng có thể thoát sang f4. Nếu Trắng đi Tượng, Đen chiếu hết bằng Nf5#.
hintsVi: Mã đen dọa chiếu hết ở f5. Vua trắng có thể rời h4 bằng nước nào?

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Nf5# relies on the pawn on h5 controlling g4 and the king on g6 controlling g5. The white pawn occupies h3. Kg3 moves toward the centre and enables Kf4 against Nf5+.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: Each of the seven other legal starts is a bishop move and allows Nf5#. There is no other legal king move.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: The fourteen legal replies after Kg3 give no immediate mate or renewed mate threat. The three checks are Nf5+, Ne4+ and h4+, each with several safe king responses. Kf4, Kf3 and Kg4 respectively are verified examples. The played Kf5 and the strong Nf7 lines were reviewed. No material offer.
reviewNotes.level: Six pieces. The only available king move is immediately visible. The learner can check why the tempting bishop moves fail.
reviewNotes.provenance: Bok–Arpith S Bijoy, 1st 3-0 Thursday 30 July 2026 round 9, The Week in Chess 1656. Replayed the original complete game to the FEN after 68...Kg6. 69.Kg3 was played. Nf5+ Kf4 is analysis.

reviews.reason: f6 defends the rook’s mating square with a pawn and permits an immediate equal recapture if White takes it.
reviews.distinctness: Pawn controls the opponent’s mating destination, instead of clearing the king’s own flight square as in the active f4 or blocking an approach as in the active h6.
reviews.solutionVi: Trắng dọa Rg5#. Đen đi f6 — Tốt từ f7 đến f6, bảo vệ ô g5. Nếu Trắng chiếu Rg5+, Đen bắt Xe bằng fxg5. Trong ván đấu, Trắng đi exf6 và Đen bắt lại Tốt bằng Kxf6.
hintsVi: Tốt đen nào có thể tiến lên để bảo vệ ô g5?

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: After Rg1, White threatens Rg5#. The pawn on f7 cannot capture the checking rook there. f6 gives the pawn direct control of g5.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: Independently replayed all ten legal moves. All nine alternatives, including a2, permit Rg5#.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: Checked all 22 legal White replies. Rg5+ has only fxg5. White can take the pawn with exf6, but Black immediately recaptures Kxf6 as in the full game. Reviewed quiet Kd4 Rd7+, Kd3 fxe5 and Kd2 a2. No reply renews an immediate mate after f6. The pawn offer is an immediate equal exchange if accepted.
reviewNotes.level: Ten pieces, but the mating rook and the pawn’s diagonal control of g5 are visible in one move.
reviewNotes.provenance: Replayed all 144 plies of Taher–Caruana from TWIC 1666. White played 53.Rg1 and Black played 53...f6, then 54.exf6 Kxf6.

reviews.reason: Kxf2 takes the unprotected rook before both black rooks can support one another on the f-file.
reviews.distinctness: A king captures one of two attackers before the other can mate. The distinction between the two possible black captures on f1 gives the learner a concrete threat to identify.
reviews.solutionVi: Đen dọa Rdxf1# — Xe từ d1 đến f1, bắt Mã và chiếu hết. Trắng đi Kxf2 — Vua từ g1 đến f2, bắt Xe hỗ trợ. Nếu Xe đen còn lại bắt Mã bằng Rxf1+, Trắng bắt Xe bằng Kxf1.
hintsVi: Xe đen ở f2 sẽ bảo vệ Xe khi quân đó sang f1. Vua trắng có thể bắt Xe ở f2 ngay không?

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Rdxf1# uses the stationary rook on f2 for protection. If the f2-rook goes to f1 instead, White can escape to g2. Kxf2 removes the supporting rook and moves the king out of the net.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All six alternatives, including Kh1 and all five pawn moves, permit Rdxf1#.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: Both forcing Black replies allow immediate recapture: Rxf1+ Kxf1 and Rd2+ Nxd2+. The strongest quiet Kf4 allows the counterplay f6 gxf6 h4 in the bounded review, and Ra1 allows Ng3+. The defence avoids mate even though the ending is still contested. No new capture offer.
reviewNotes.level: Ten pieces and one direct king capture. The attacked king can safely take the rook on f2.
reviewNotes.provenance: Complete Perske–Englert game, 43rd Münsterland Open, Münster, 18 October 2026, TWIC 1667. Original position follows 41...Rxf2. The game played 42.Kxf2 Kf4 43.Kg2. The recaptures after checks are analysis.

reviews.reason: Kh6 opens g7 against Rh1+. Kh4 fails because the white pawn already occupies the potential escape g3.
reviews.distinctness: The earlier comparison with Petrosian–Karpov was against an unpublished position. The closest published exercise, Andreikin–Artemiev, uses a rook check from the opposite end of the board and an opposing king that controls the wrong escape. Here White must notice that its own g3-pawn occupies that escape.
reviews.solutionVi: Kh6 — Vua trắng từ h5 đến h6. Nếu Đen chiếu Rh1+, Vua trắng thoát qua g7. Đi h4 vẫn cho phép Rh1# vì Tốt trắng ở g3 chiếm ô thoát của Vua.
hintsVi: Xe đen dọa chiếu hết ở h1. Hãy so sánh h4 và h6, chú ý Tốt trắng đang đứng ở g3.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Black threatens Rh1#. Kh6 makes g7 available. If White chooses Kh4, the black king controls the flights g4 and g5, and the white pawn occupies g3.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All ten alternatives allow Rh1#, including Kh4 and f4. The same legal mating reply was verified independently for every alternative.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: Black has no immediate mate after Kh6. The only check Rh1+ has the sole evasion Kg7. The only capture Rxb7 permits the immediate Rxb7, and the strong Rb5 and played Rb2 alternatives were reviewed without renewed mate. Kh6 creates no offer.
reviewNotes.level: Nine pieces. The choice is a direct comparison of the two h-file king moves. The defender’s own pawn is the relevant obstruction.
reviewNotes.provenance: Radjabov–Christiansen, Titled Tuesday Late 28 November 2023 round 4, PGN Mentor Radjabov archive. Complete game and unmodified FEN after 55...Rb1 verified. 56.Kh6 was played. Rh1+ Kg7 is analysis.

reviews.reason: Nxf2 alone removes the pawn controlling the white king’s two escape squares against Ng3#.
reviews.distinctness: Captures the stationary pawn guard rather than the checking knight. Unlike the active Kxa2, the captured pawn is a mate helper, with the knight still able to give check.
reviews.solutionVi: Đen dọa Ng3#. Trắng đi Nxf2 — Mã từ d1 đến f2, bắt Tốt đen đang khống chế e1 và g1. Nếu Đen vẫn chiếu Ng3+, Vua trắng có thể thoát sang e1 hoặc g1.
hintsVi: Nếu Mã đen đến g3, quân đen nào đang khống chế cả e1 và g1?

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Ne2 prepares Ng3#. The pawn f2 covers e1 and g1, leaving no king escape. Nxf2 removes that guard and keeps the white knight protected by Kf1.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: Independently replayed all four legal roots. Nc3, Nb2 and Ne3 each allow Ng3#.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: Checked all nine Black replies. The only check Ng3+ allows Ke1 or Kg1, each safe from mate on the next move. The quiet Nf4 allows Ke1, Nc1 allows Nh3 and Nc3 allows Nd3. After Nf4 Ke1 Nd3+ Kd1 Kxf2, only the black king and knight remain against the white king and there is no mating material. No reply renews an immediate mate and Black cannot capture the white knight immediately.
reviewNotes.level: Five pieces and a direct capture to create two king escapes. No sacrifice or preparation is required.
reviewNotes.provenance: Replayed all 141 plies of Darvishi–Shimanov from TWIC 1660. Black played 70...Ne2 and White played 71.Nxf2, the last move in the recorded draw.

reviews.reason: Kd1 is the sole defence and creates a route to c2 against the rook’s back-rank check.
reviews.distinctness: The white bishop and king seal the adjacent escape squares. The learner must compare the two opposite king steps from e1, in a six-piece position with the threatened king on a central file.
reviews.solutionVi: Trắng dọa Rh1#. Đen đi Kd1 — Vua từ e1 đến d1. Sau Rh1+, Vua đen thoát chiếu bằng Kc2. Nếu đi Kf1, Đen vẫn bị chiếu hết bằng Rh1#.
hintsVi: Khi Xe trắng chiếu ở h1, Vua đen cần đứng ở đâu để có thể thoát sang c2?

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: The bishop on e3 controls d2 and f2, and the white king on f3 covers e2 and f2. Kd1 makes c2 available against Rh1+.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All 12 other legal starting moves, including Kf1 and every rook move, allow Rh1#.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: Rh1+ allows only Kc2. White can then take on b1 and Black can immediately recapture with Kxb1. Rd2+ allows Kc1, with Ke1 also legal. Strong quiet Bg5 and Ra2 allow Rb3+ and Rb3, respectively. No relevant new capture offer follows Kd1.
reviewNotes.level: Six pieces and one direct quiet king move, with no sacrifice. Kf1 makes a clear beginner comparison.
reviewNotes.provenance: Complete Weetik–Wanyama game, Titled Tuesday, 21 July 2026, TWIC 1655. Original position follows 84.Rh2. The game played 84...Kd1 85.Rf2 Ke1. Rh1+ Kc2 is analysis.

reviews.reason: g4 clears g5 and keeps the f7-pawn guarding g6. The alternatives f5 and f6 each open a second immediate knight mate. White can take the offered pawn only as an even exchange.
reviews.distinctness: The prior Karpov–Bacrot clearance offers only bishop moves as alternatives. Here the learner compares three pawn moves, seeing how the wrong pawn move gives the knight another mating square. The real game also shows the pawn exchange and a king recapture.
reviews.solutionVi: g4 — Tốt đen từ g5 đến g4, nhường ô g5 cho Vua. Nếu Trắng chiếu Nf5+, Vua đen thoát qua g5. Trong ván đấu, Trắng bắt Tốt bằng hxg4 và Đen bắt lại bằng Kxg4.
hintsVi: Mã trắng dọa Nf5#. Tốt đen nào có thể nhường ô thoát cho Vua mà vẫn giữ Tốt f7 bảo vệ g6?

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: White threatens Nf5#. The g5-pawn blocks the black king’s flight. g4 opens g5 while the f7-pawn still guards g6 against Ng6+.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: Independent legal replay checked all sixteen starting moves. The thirteen bishop moves allow Nf5#. f6 allows both Nf5# and Ng6#. f5 allows both Nxf5# and Ng6#.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: All eleven replies leave no immediate mate after g4. Nf5+ has the sole escape Kg5. Ng6+ allows fxg6 or Kg5. hxg4 can be answered by hxg4 or Kxg4, both immediately recovering the pawn. The game used Kxg4. The strongest quiet Nc6 and Nd5 lines allow gxh3+ and viable play.
reviewNotes.level: Nine pieces. The one pawn step opens a visible flight. The two immediate recaptures make the exchange clear.
reviewNotes.provenance: Vokhidov–Kamsky, Korchnoi Memorial Open, St Petersburg 2018 round 7.9, PGN Mentor Kamsky archive. Complete game and original FEN after 87.Ne7 verified. 87...g4 88.hxg4 Kxg4 was played. Nf5+ Kg5 is analysis.

reviews.reason: Kg6 makes a pawn interposition available against the threatened bishop mate. The original check now has the safe reply f5.
reviews.distinctness: The defending king steps farther down the bishop’s diagonal so that its pawn can block the check. The active discovered-bishop-mate example Klukin–Bok leaves the diagonal entirely. Neither the active nor pending set has this king-and-pawn block.
reviews.solutionVi: Kg6 — Vua đen từ f5 đến g6, nhường ô f5 cho Tốt. Nếu Trắng chiếu Bd3+, Đen đẩy Tốt từ f6 đến f5 để chắn chiếu. Nếu Trắng bắt Tốt bằng Bxf5+, Vua đen bắt lại Tượng bằng Kxf5.
hintsVi: Tượng trắng dọa chiếu hết từ d3. Vua đen có thể đi đâu để Tốt f6 chắn được đường chéo chiếu Vua?

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: White threatens Bd3# against the king on f5. Kg6 vacates f5 while staying on the same diagonal. If White checks on d3, Black blocks with f6–f5.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All thirteen other legal roots permit Bd3#, including Bxd6 and rook moves such as Re8. Kg6 is the sole legal king move.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: Checked all 34 legal White replies and four checks. Bd3+ has the sole response f5. If White immediately takes the blocker with Bxf5+, Kxf5 wins the bishop for the pawn. Re6+ after the block allows Kf7. Other checks have safe direct responses, including Rg7+ Kxg7, Bf7+ Rxf7 and f5+ Kxf5. No offer or renewed immediate mate after Kg6.
reviewNotes.level: Nine pieces. A single king step enables a clear pawn block if the threatened check is tried. No second preparation or sacrifice is needed.
reviewNotes.provenance: Zhong–Mu, Xinghua CCA Master 2026 round 5.10, The Week in Chess 1667. Complete game replay reached the original FEN after 74.Re7. 74...Kg6 was played. The immediate Bd3+ f5 illustration is analysis.

reviews.reason: b4+ gives check and clears b3, the flight square against the two-rook mating attack. Every king reply leaves that square safe.
reviews.distinctness: A pawn vacates the king’s escape square while giving check. Existing f4 clearance is quiet, and existing counterchecks are played by rooks.
reviews.solutionVi: b4+ — Tốt trắng từ b3 đến b4 chiếu Vua và nhường ô b3 cho Vua trắng. Trong ván đấu, Đen đáp Kb5. Nếu Xe đen có dịp chiếu Rxa2+ sau đó, Vua trắng đã có ô b3 để thoát. Nếu Trắng đi Bxf7 ngay, Đen chiếu hết bằng Rxa2#.
hintsVi: Tốt trắng ở b3 có thể chiếu Vua đen và nhường ô thoát cho Vua trắng bằng nước nào?

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Rxa2# is an exact mate threat. b4+ gives check and clears b3, the flight square against the two-rook mating attack. Every king reply leaves that square safe.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: Exhaustive replay verifies immediate mate after the other 19 legal moves.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: Kb5, Kb6 and Ka6 are all legal replies. After each, Kb3 is available against Rxa2+ in the threat probe. White’s king on a3 guards the pawn on b4, and the opponent cannot capture it. No material offer.
reviewNotes.level: One direct learner decision from a legal 9-piece game position.
reviewNotes.provenance: Starozhilov,L–Kengurov,Yaroslav, Titled Tue 6th Oct 2026, 2026.10.06, source ply 100. Original FEN and preceding move reproduced. b4+ was played. https://theweekinchess.com/zips/twic1666g.zip

reviews.reason: White needs five moves against the strong played replies. The rook sacrifice clears a8 to promote with check, and the later queen sacrifice removes the rook behind the mating pawn.
reviews.distinctness: Two accepted sacrifices with different purposes. White makes a promotion square available with tempo, then uses the newly promoted queen to dismantle the mating net.
reviews.solutionVi: Đen dọa g5#. Trắng thí Xe bằng 52.Rg8+ để dọn ô a8. Sau 52...Kxg8 53.a8=Q+ Kg7, Trắng đi 54.Qd8, đưa Hậu lên đường chéo d8–g5. Khi Đen chiếu 54...g5+, Trắng thí Hậu bằng 55.Qxg5+. Sau 55...Rxg5 56.Kxg5, đòn chiếu hết được hóa giải. Hai bên còn Mã và số Tốt bằng nhau.
hintsVi: Nước chiếu nào vừa dọn ô a8, vừa cho Trắng thời gian phong cấp?
Sau khi phong Hậu, tìm ô trên đường chéo dẫn đến g5 để có thể bắt Tốt khi Đen chiếu.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: White is facing g5#, with the rook on g1 and knight on f4 covering the escape squares. Rg8+ offers a whole rook without an immediate recapture and makes a8 available. The promotion restores material with tempo. Qd8 prepares Qxg5+ after the renewed pawn check. If Black captures the new queen, Kxg5 removes the attacking rook and leaves equal nominal material.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: Independent root replay found g5# after all 11 initial alternatives. After Kxg8, a8=Q+ is the only sound promotion. A bounded exhaustive mate search refuted a8=R+ in three black moves. After Kg7, 14 alternatives give immediate g5#. Bounded exhaustive search refuted Qh8+, Qg8+ and Qf8+ in two black moves, and the stored all-root engine comparison found Qa1+ decisively inferior. Qxg5+ is the only legal reply to g5+. At the final decision, only Kxg5 recovers the rook and remains sound. Stopping earlier leaves mate pressure or a whole-rook deficit.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: Kxg8 is strongest after Rg8+. Both Kg7 and Kh7 after promotion allow Qd8 and the same defence to g5+. After Qd8, g5+ is the strongest reply, while Rh1+ allows Kg3, Ng2+ also allows Kg3, and Rg4+ allows Kxg4. After Qxg5+, Black can insert Ng6+. White can answer Kh5 and still recapture after Rxg5+, with the bounded engine line near equality. After the main line Kxg5, Ne6+ and Nh3+ both leave four mate-safe king evasions, and the strongest quiet replies are playable. All legal replies at every sample decision were screened, with every check and capture covered in the deep reply evidence.
reviewNotes.level: Five necessary White moves against the strongest played branch. There is no immediate recapture after the first rook is taken. The later unequal trade resolves the renewed pawn mate and leaves two knights and four pawns total. Later knight checks do not restart the mating net.
reviewNotes.provenance: Complete Spizharny–Vershinin game, Rogachev Masters, Rahachow, 30 July 2026, TWIC 1656. Original FEN follows 51...Nf4. Every move in the nine-ply sample was played. Other cited variations are analysis.

reviews.reason: The accepted pawn offer opens the only escape from the first rook check. A strong checking sequence requires four black moves, and the active king and pieces compensate for the pawn after Ke4.
reviews.distinctness: A clearance sacrifice for king mobility under alternating rook checks. Its material cost is smaller than the double-sacrifice example, but the king must choose a sound route through the checking sequence and leave the offered pawn behind.
reviews.solutionVi: Trắng dọa Rh8#. Đen đi 42...g5, thí Tốt để mở ô g6 cho Vua. Sau 43.Rh8+ Kg6 44.Rg8+ Kf5 45.Rxg5+ Ke4, Vua đen thoát chuỗi chiếu và bảo vệ Xe ở f4. Nếu Trắng tiếp tục tấn công Xe bằng 46.Rg4, Đen có thể đổi Xe bằng 46...Rxg4.
hintsVi: Tốt nào đang chiếm ô Vua đen cần dùng để thoát đòn Rh8#?
Sau khi nhường ô g6, hãy tính đường đi của Vua khi Xe trắng đổi sang cột g và bắt Tốt có chiếu.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: White threatens Rh8#, with Bf6 guarding both the rook on h8 and the escape square g7, while the black pawn occupies g6. g5 opens g6 and offers a pawn that White can take immediately with Bxg5. In the stronger checking line White takes it with Rxg5+ and Black cannot recapture. Ke4 escapes the final rook check and protects Rf4.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: Independent enumeration found 16 of 20 first moves allow Rh8#. Rxf6 and Bg1+ are decisively inferior in the all-root comparison. Rf2+ is sound but still requires g5 against Kg3. Independent 700,000-node all-root probes found only g5 playable after Rf2+ Kg3, with a strong continuation Kg4 Kg6 Rg8+ still requiring a fourth black move. Kg6 is the only reply to Rh8+. After Rg8+, Kf5 and Kh5 are sound, but both allow Rxg5+ and still need a fourth move, Ke4 or Kh6 respectively. Kh7 and Kh6 are inferior in the all-root probe.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: After g5, Rh8+ is the strongest played reply and Bxg5 allows Re4 in the shorter branch. After Kg6, Rg8+ is strongest, while Bxg5 allows Kxg5 and Rh6+ allows Kxh6. After Kf5, Rxg5+ forces Ke4, and Bxg5 allows Rf2+ counterplay. There are no forcing White replies from the endpoint. The independent 700,000-node all-root probe after quiet Rg4 found both Rxg4 and Bxe5 playable, and the source game played Rxg4. The endpoint is sound in bounded evidence while down one pawn. It makes no claim of a forced draw.
reviewNotes.level: Four necessary black moves against the strongest checking branch. The deliberately exposed pawn is taken without immediate recovery. The move order and king route have to account for sustained checks and compensation from the active king, rook and bishop. This is the lower material-cost D case.
reviewNotes.provenance: Complete Oleksiyenko–Ter Sahakyan game, 3-0 Thursday, 29 October 2026, TWIC 1669. Original FEN follows 42.Bf6. All seven plies in the sample were played, followed by 46.Rg4 Rxg4. Other cited lines are analysis.

reviews.reason: The rook sacrifice removes the pawn and displaces the attacking king. White then needs a pawn tempo and two consecutive king moves against renewed mate threats before the surviving passed pawn can recover the sacrificed material.
reviews.distinctness: A rook sacrifice creates time for connected passed pawns, while repeated first-rank mate threats force the king to change its escape square twice. Promotion is the necessary material recovery after the opposing rook takes the other pawn.
reviews.solutionVi: 46.Rxg3+ — Xe trắng từ h3 bắt Tốt ở g3 và chiếu, buộc Vua đen rời f3. Trong ván đấu, Đen nhận thí Xe bằng 46...Kxg3 và Trắng đi 47.b7. Sau 47...Kf3, Đen lại dọa Rc1#. Trắng đi 48.Ke1 để có đường thoát qua d2. Đen đáp 48...Ke3, khống chế d2, nên Trắng đi 49.Kd1 để có thể bắt Xe nếu Xe chiếu ở c1. Sau 49...Rxc6, Tốt còn lại phong Hậu bằng 50.b8=Q.
hintsVi: Đen dọa Rc1#. Tìm nước chiếu vừa bắt Tốt g3, vừa buộc Vua đen rời f3.
Tính cách giữ hai Tốt thông. Nếu Vua đen trở lại f3 rồi tiến đến e3, Vua trắng phải đổi ô thoát như thế nào?

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Black threatens Rc1#. Rxg3+ removes the g3-pawn and displaces the f3-king. After Kxg3, b7 preserves promotion counterplay. Kf3 renews Rc1#, Ke1 makes Kd2 available, and Ke3 then covers d2. Kd1 makes Kxc1 possible. Rxc6 removes one passed pawn, so b8=Q recovers the rook sacrifice.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: Ten of twelve initial roots allow immediate Rc1#. Immediate Ke1 survives that specific mate but Rc1+ Kd2 Rxc6 loses the connected-pawn compensation, with the bounded score decisively worse. After Kxg3, immediate Ke1 fails to Rxc6 followed by Rxb6, and Kg1 permits Rc1#. c7 is also sound, but a strong Kf3 keeps the defence and recovery at least as long. At move 48, the drawing alternative Kg1 Rb2 needs c7 as the sole non-losing continuation and then Kh2 as the sole legal reply to Rb1+, reaching its critical defence on the fifth solver move. At move 49 Kf1 Rb2 c7 Rxb7 c8=Q likewise does not shorten recovery.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: Kxg3 is the strongest acceptance. The rook for a pawn costs 400 on the project scale and has no immediate recapture. The weaker Kf4 and Ke4 permit prompt pawn advances. On the played route, both Kf3 and Ke3 renew Rc1#. After Kd1, Rd2+ and Rb2 have sound continuations that preserve promotion. Rxc6 is met by b8=Q, and the strongest bounded replies Rc4, Kd3, Rc5, Kd4 and Ke4 renew no forcing mate. A targeted full seven-root replay at 2.5 million Stockfish nodes after 48.Kg1 Rb2 found c7 the only non-losing move. Legal generation verifies Kh2 as the sole evasion after Rb1+.
reviewNotes.level: Five solver moves under the played strong continuation. The king moves are meaningful defenses to the same renewed mate on different escape squares. The fifth move restores material after the rook sacrifice. No shorter sound defense was found against the strong alternatives reviewed.
reviewNotes.provenance: Pribelszky–Bologan, Titled Tuesday 17 March 2026 round 7, PGN Mentor Bologan archive. Complete source replay reaches the unmodified FEN after 45...Kf3. The full proposed line through 50.b8=Q was played.

reviews.reason: The g-pawn is genuinely given up to dislodge the king. Rook and queen counterchecks then switch lines until the white queen guards the mating square.
reviews.distinctness: Counterchecks relocate the black king while the white queen changes diagonal and secures h1.
reviews.solutionVi: Đen dọa chiếu hết bằng Qh1#. Trắng chiếu Qh8+. Sau Kf5, Trắng thí Tốt bằng g4+ để kéo Vua đen đến g4. Tiếp theo là Rd4+ Kf3, rồi Qa8+. Sau Ke2, đường chéo a8–h1 mở ra. Nếu Đen chiếu Qh1+, Trắng đổi Hậu bằng Qxh1 Rxh1+ Kxh1 và hóa giải đòn tấn công.
hintsVi: Đen dọa Qh1#. Trắng có thể bắt đầu chuỗi chiếu từ ô nào?
Sau Kf5, hãy tìm nước thí Tốt để đưa Vua đen vào tầm chiếu của Xe.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: The opponent threatens Qh1#. Qh8+ interrupts the first threat, g4+ pulls the king to g4, Rd4+ forces it away, and Qa8+ opens the a8–h1 diagonal once Black replies Ke2.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: The full root comparisons find Qh8+, g4+ and Rd4+ as the sole viable moves in their respective sample positions. Rf4+ is a comparable fourth-move option, so the published sample is one solution.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: Ke7 preserves the original threat and requires a different countercheck. hxg4 after g4+ threatens Qg1# and permits e4+. After Kxg4 and Rd4+ the strongest Kf3 still threatens Qh1#. In the played line after Qa8+ Ke2, Qh1+ is now answered by Qxh1 Rxh1+ Kxh1. The pawn is positional compensation for breaking the mating net.
reviewNotes.level: Four solver moves against strong replies. The first three leave a concrete mate threat after the sample reply. Qa8+ gives the queen the defensive diagonal that was unavailable earlier.
reviewNotes.provenance: Almasi,Z–Dubov,Daniil, 21st European Teams, 2017.10.31. Exact source position and preceding move replayed at ply 84. Sample fully played. https://www.pgnmentor.com/players/Almasi.zip

reviews.reason: Removing the first rook makes the later queen offer viable. The acceptance transfers the mating support to f7 and forces a king recapture, after which the strongest queen check leaves exactly two legal evasions.
reviews.distinctness: First remove one of two attacking rooks, then offer the queen to draw the remaining rook onto a square the defending king can capture. The king accepts exposure as the cost of stopping the mating attack.
reviews.solutionVi: 34...Nxd7 — Mã đen từ b6 bắt Xe ở d7. Trắng bắt lại bằng 35.Rxd7 và vẫn dọa Qg7#. Đen đi 35...Qf7, thí Hậu để kéo Xe đến f7. Sau 36.Rxf7, Đen phải bắt Xe bằng 36...Kxf7 để ngăn Qg7# và Qxh7#. Trong ván đấu, Trắng chiếu 37.Qxh7+ và Vua đen thoát chiếu bằng 37...Ke6. Vua đen cũng có thể đi 37...Kf8.
hintsVi: Trắng dọa Qg7#. Xe nào đang bảo vệ g7, và Đen có thể bắt Xe đó bằng quân nào?
Sau khi Xe trắng thứ hai đến d7, Đen có thể kéo Xe đến ô nào để Vua đen bắt được?

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: White’s Qg7# is supported by the rook on d7. Nxd7 removes that rook, but Rxd7 replaces it. Qf7 interposes on the rook’s seventh-rank line. Rxf7 restores the support from f7 and adds Qxh7#. Kxf7 removes the support. The strongly preferred Qxh7+ then forces Kf8 or Ke6 to get out of check.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All forty legal starting moves independently replayed. Thirty-four allow immediate mate. The direct Qf7 leaves an additional white rook and is decisively inferior after Rxf7 Kxf7 Qxh7+, and Re7 loses to Rxe7. The three counterchecks also fail in the bounded comparison. After Rxd7, Qf7 is the sole viable root; after Rxf7, all nineteen alternatives to Kxf7 allow immediate mate. Both Kf8 and Ke6 are sound final evasions, with no earlier equivalent endpoint.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: Rxf7 is the strongest reply to Qf7. The queen offer loses 900 on acceptance and Kxf7 recovers only a rook, a net 400 against the local material balance. This is a real cost after the earlier rook-for-knight sequence. White’s Qxh7+ after Kxf7 is more than one pawn stronger in the bounded evidence than the next reply. Qg7+ allows Kxg7, Qxg6+ allows hxg6, and Qf8+ allows Rxf8. After Ke6 the main pressure is pawn capture Qxg6, and neither that nor the other strong replies renews the immediate attack. The two rooks give playable compensation without any claim of a game-theoretic result.
reviewNotes.level: Four connected solver moves under the strongest reviewed continuation. The terminal king evasion is required by the sole comparably strong reply, and there are exactly two legal answers. The independent sacrifice is the queen for one rook, separate from the initial rook-for-knight exchange.
reviewNotes.provenance: Bacrot–Makarian, Titled Tuesday Early 4 October 2022 round 7, PGN Mentor Bacrot archive. Exact complete replay reaches the original FEN after 34.Rd7. The full selected line through 37...Ke6 was played. Kf8 is verified analysis.

reviews.reason: Bxf7+ sacrifices the bishop to clear c4 for the knight. White then survives the queen capture while keeping b2 covered and takes the opposing queen on its fourth move. The strongest recapture leaves no continued forcing attack.
reviews.distinctness: Bishop clearance sacrifice for a knight to defend b2 and attack the opposing queen simultaneously, followed by queen recovery after a checking capture of White's queen.
reviews.solutionVi: Đen dọa Qb2#. Trắng đi Bxf7+ — Tượng từ c4 đến f7, bắt Tốt và chiếu, nhường ô c4 cho Mã. Sau Kxf7, Nc4 vừa bảo vệ b2 vừa tấn công Hậu đen ở a3. Đen đáp Nxd2+, bắt Hậu trắng và chiếu. Trong phương án phân tích, Trắng đi Bxd2, giữ Mã ở c4. Sau Rhd8, Trắng bắt Hậu đen bằng Nxa3. Nếu Đen đáp bxa3, hai Hậu đều đã rời bàn cờ và vật chất trở lại gần cân bằng. Trong ván đấu, Trắng bắt lại bằng Rxd2 ở nước 20.
hintsVi: Quân trắng nào đang chiếm ô c4? Từ c4, Mã b6 có thể vừa giữ b2 vừa tấn công a3.
Nếu Mã đen bắt Hậu ở d2 và chiếu, hãy tìm cách bắt lại mà vẫn giữ Mã trắng ở c4.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Black's Nxe4 leaves the immediate threat Qb2#. Bxf7+ clears the square c4 with tempo, accepting Kxf7 for a bishop net of the pawn. Nc4 then guards b2 and attacks Qa3, so Nxd2+ can be met without moving that knight.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: Independently checked the legal root sets and immediate mate refutations for all 129 solver roots across the four steps. Forty of the fifty initial moves allow mate in one. Alternatives Nd3, Na4, c3 and Bd4 avoid the initial mate but let Black take the queen with Nxd2+ without the same recovery. On move three, Nxd2 allows Qb2#, while Rxd2 is also sound and still requires the fourth-move queen recovery in the strong Bc3 line. After Bxd2 Rhd8, h5 and Nd3 in the engine lines only delay taking Qa3. Bc1 Qxc1+ Kxc1 would recover the queen on a fifth solver move.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: Replayed every screened line for all 137 opponent replies on the four sample turns, including Kf8 as the sacrifice decline, Nxd2+ as the strongest challenge, and Nc3+ Qxc3 Bxc3 Nxa3 as a secondary forcing queen-recovery branch. After Bxd2, a5 and Rhd8 both allow Nxa3. In the reviewed sample, 21.Nxa3 bxa3 returns material to within 10 nominal cp and leaves neither check nor a pending mate in one. Of the 29 legal White continuations, 28 avoid immediate mate. The threat has subsided, with ordinary play such as Bc1 or h5 available.
reviewNotes.level: Four connected solver moves. After the accepted bishop sacrifice, Nc4 removes the renewed threat, Bxd2 handles a check while keeping b2 defended, and Nxa3 is necessary for the sample to regain the captured queen. At the third move White is still down its queen for the recaptured knight, so stopping there would omit a decisive recovery rather than trim padding.
reviewNotes.provenance: Replayed all 132 plies of Jia–Firouzja from TWIC 1660. Black played 17...Nxe4. The game and sample match through 18.Bxf7+ Kxf7 19.Nc4 Nxd2+. White played 20.Rxd2, so 20.Bxd2 Rhd8 21.Nxa3 is explicitly marked analysis.

reviews.reason: Four White moves are needed against the strong played checking sequence. White gives up the queen for a rook to escape the original net, then coordinates both rooks to close the remaining line of check.
reviews.distinctness: The queen counterchecks while removing the attacking rook. The later interposition on d2 works because the white king and the second rook both guard d2.
reviews.solutionVi: Trắng đang bị Xe c7 chiếu. Trắng thí Hậu bằng 57.Qxc7+, bắt Xe và chiếu lại. Sau 57...Qxc7+ 58.Kb3 Qb6+ 59.Kc2 Qf2+, Trắng đi 60.Rd2 để chặn chiếu. Vua c2 và Xe d8 cùng bảo vệ Xe d2. Nếu Đen bắt Xe bằng Qxd2+, Trắng có thể bắt Hậu bằng Kxd2.
hintsVi: Nước nào vừa bắt Xe đang chiếu ở c7, vừa chiếu lại Vua đen?
Khi Hậu đen chiếu từ f2, Xe trắng có thể chặn ở ô nào mà vẫn được Vua và Xe còn lại bảo vệ?

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Qxc7+ removes the rook checking from c7 and counterchecks. When Black answers Qxc7+, White concedes queen for rook without an immediate recapture. Kb3 and Kc2 avoid the queen’s two ensuing checks and let Rd2 interpose on a square guarded by the king and the other rook.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: Kd5 allows Qc5# immediately. An independent exhaustive search proved mate in three for Black after Qc5. Supplemental 1.8M-node probes found Kb4 inferior after Qxc7+ Qxc7+, and Qe7+ still forces further pressure if White tries it. After Qb6+, the targeted Ka3 comparison was also inferior. The full-root probe against Qf2+ found Rd2 the only defence within the playable score threshold, with every king move worse.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: Qxc7+ is the strongest reply to the countercheck. After Kb3, both Qb6+ and Qf7+ are strong, with the latter allowing R3d5. After Kc2, Qf2+ is strong alongside quiet Ne6 and Kg7. At Rd2 the serious replies Qf3, Qc5, Qf1, Qf6 and Qf7 are quiet and allow continued defence. Qxd2+ allows Kxd2 or Rxd2, while Qxg3 allows Rxf8. Every legal reply was screened, and every check and capture was included in the deep evidence.
reviewNotes.level: Four necessary solver moves in the played branch, with a genuine four-point queen-for-rook loss and coordination of the king and both rooks. The endpoint has sustainable defensive resources in bounded evidence. The result of the source game is separate from the tactical objective.
reviewNotes.provenance: Complete Movahed–Niemann game, Esports World Cup B, Paris, 13 August 2026, TWIC 1658. Original FEN follows 56...Rc7+. All seven sample plies were played, followed by 60...Qf3. Qxd2+ Kxd2 is analysis.

reviews.reason: White must sacrifice the queen for a rook and pawn, then answer a strong chain of queen checks with two defended interpositions. Neither retreat at the first check nor a king move at the third and fourth decisions provides the same viable defence.
reviews.distinctness: A queen offer captures the checking pawn, followed by king recapture and interpositions by two different pieces on perpendicular lines. Movahed–Niemann also has a queen sacrifice and d2 interposition, but here both Rc4 and Bd2 are essential against different queen checks, and the first move captures a pawn rather than a rook.
reviews.solutionVi: 31.Qxc2 — Hậu trắng từ e4 bắt Tốt ở c2 để giải chiếu. Đen nhận thí Hậu bằng 31...Rxc2 và dọa Qa2#. Trắng bắt lại Xe bằng 32.Kxc2. Sau 32...Qc5+, 33.Rc4 chắn chiếu và Tốt b3 bảo vệ Xe. Đen chiếu tiếp 33...Qf2+. Trắng đi 34.Bd2, dùng Tượng chắn đường chiếu trên hàng hai. Nếu Hậu đen bắt Tượng bằng Qxd2+, Vua trắng bắt lại Hậu.
hintsVi: Nếu Vua trắng đi Kb2, Hậu đen có thể chiếu hết ở đâu? Tìm nước khác để giải chiếu.
Sau khi Vua trắng bắt lại Xe ở c2, hãy tìm hai nước chắn chiếu. Mỗi quân dùng để chắn cần được bảo vệ.

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: White is checked by the pawn on c2. Kb2 permits Qa3#. Qxc2 is the sole answer that avoids mate. After the rook accepts on c2, Kxc2 removes the piece supporting Qa2#. Rc4 blocks the c-file check with a rook supported by b3, and Bd2 blocks the second-rank check with a bishop supported by the king.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: All legal roots were independently checked at every frame. After Rxc2, the other four non-mating roots Rd8+, Ra4, Ba3 and Bb2 all give decisively inferior results. After Qc5+, the five king moves all fare substantially worse than Rc4. After Qf2+, the best retreat Kb1 is still over a pawn worse than Bd2, while the other three king moves are decisively worse. No shorter viable answer to the forcing continuation.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: Rxc2 is the strongest acceptance and leaves a fresh Qa2# threat. The initial queen offer costs 800 after capturing the pawn and then recovers a rook with Kxc2, a net 300 compared with the starting balance. Against Rc4 the queen check Qf2+ evaluates within five centipawns of the best quiet Qd5, so the final interposition is required against a fully competitive reply. Qxc4+ bxc4 and Qxd2+ Kxd2 verify that the blockers are defended and not further sacrifices. After Bd2 the strong a5, Kh7, Bh4 and Bc5 do not renew forcing pressure.
reviewNotes.level: Four necessary solver moves against the strong checking branch. The initial queen offer is genuine and accepted, and the two protected blockers form a connected tactical defence. The endpoint remains playable under the strongest bounded replies.
reviewNotes.provenance: Leko–Anand, Dortmund Semi-Finals 2004 round 4, PGN Mentor Leko archive. Complete game replay reaches the original FEN after 30...c2+. The full selected line through 34.Bd2 was played.

reviews.reason: Four Black moves are needed in the played branch. Black gives up the h8-rook to save the king, then coordinates the remaining rook and king to remove the attackers.
reviews.distinctness: The two connected rook decisions handle different mating squares. One rook takes the pawn controlling the king’s escape and later removes the knight that supports the renewed mate.
reviews.solutionVi: Trắng dọa Rb8#. Đen đi 41...Rxe6, bắt Tốt đang khống chế d7. Sau 42.Rb8+, Đen đi 42...Kd7, chấp nhận thí Xe ở h8. Trắng đi 43.Rxh8 và dọa Rd8#. Đen đáp 43...Rxc6, bắt Mã đang bảo vệ d8. Sau 44.Bxc6+ Kxc6, Đen đã loại bỏ cả Mã lẫn Tượng và hóa giải đòn chiếu hết.
hintsVi: Quân trắng nào đang khống chế d7, ô Vua đen cần dùng để thoát chiếu?
Sau khi Xe trắng bắt ở h8, quân nào đang bảo vệ d8 cho đòn chiếu hết tiếp theo?

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: White threatens Rb8# because the knight covers b8 and d8 and the e6-pawn controls d7. Rxe6 clears the king’s exit. Kd7 leaves the h8-rook to be taken without an immediate recapture. Rxc6 removes the knight supporting the renewed Rd8# threat. Kxc6 then takes the bishop and restores sufficient compensation.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: Every one of the 17 initial alternatives allows Rb8#. Kd7 is the only legal reply to Rb8+. After Rxh8, the playable alternatives Ne4, Kd6, Rf6, Re8 and Rd6 all leave strong checks in independent 1M-node all-root reply probes and retain both enemy minor pieces at that point. After Bxc6+, every king move except Kxc6 fails the bounded score threshold and leaves the bishop intact.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: After Rxe6, Rb8+ is strongest and the other checks Ne7+ and Na7+ allow Rxe7 and Kd7 respectively. After Kd7, Rxh8 is clearly strongest. After Rxc6, Bxc6+, Rxh4 and Rh7+ are comparable. Rxh4 allows Nf5 and Rh7+ allows Kd6, with the rook and king still able to remove the bishop if it captures on c6. After Kxc6, the strongest Kxh4 and Rxh4 both allow Nf5 or Nf5+ as appropriate, and the serious quiet replies leave a playable knight-and-pawns versus rook ending. Every legal reply was screened and all checks and captures received deeper coverage.
reviewNotes.level: Four solver moves against the played strongest branch, an accepted whole-rook sacrifice, and a second exchange in which the defending king removes the last minor attacker. The final pressure has changed to ordinary endgame play.
reviewNotes.provenance: Complete Steinitz–Minchin game, Great Britain tour simultaneous exhibition, 1871, Steinitz archive. Original position follows 41.dxe6. All seven sample plies were played.

reviews.reason: Bh6 offers a bishop to force a queen interposition and then an exchange of queens.
reviews.distinctness: A bishop block gives the attacking queen access to h6, where Black can block again with the queen and exchange it.
reviews.solutionVi: Trắng dọa Qxg7#. Đen đi 44...Kh8. Sau 45.Qh5+, Đen thí Tượng bằng 45...Bh6 để chặn cột h. Trắng bắt Tượng bằng 46.Qxh6+. Đen chặn chiếu bằng 46...Qh7, rồi đáp 47.Qxh7+ bằng 47...Kxh7. Đổi Hậu giúp Đen thoát đòn tấn công.
hintsVi: Nếu Hậu trắng chiếu từ h5, quân đen nào có thể chắn cột h?
Sau khi Tượng bị bắt, Đen có thể đưa Hậu đến ô nào để đổi Hậu?

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: Qxg7# is the initial threat. Kh8 meets it but the best Qh5+ renews the attack. Bh6 blocks the h-file and offers the bishop.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: Only Kh8 is viable at the start. Bh6, Qh7 and Kxh7 are individually the only legal responses to the next three checks in the played sample.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: White can decline Bh6 with Rg6, when Black has playable rook checks. The actual Qxh6+ Qh7 Qxh7+ Kxh7 exchanges queens. Best remaining Be4+ permits both Kh6 (−34) and Kh8 (−37) in supplemental full-root 500k review.
reviewNotes.level: Four necessary solver moves on the strong checking continuation, with a meaningful bishop sacrifice and an exact liquidation of the attacking queens.
reviewNotes.provenance: Grischuk,A–Balakrishnan,Praveen, Titled Tue 30th Apr Early, 2024.04.30. Full played sample and exact preceding move at source ply 87. https://www.pgnmentor.com/players/Grischuk.zip

reviews.reason: Ke5 accepts a bishop loss to avoid mate, then Rh1 secures a promotion exchange that regains the minor piece. A relevant strong check adds a fifth defensive move, and the final capture and recapture settle the tactical phase.
reviews.distinctness: King escape deliberately abandons a bishop, and the rook supports a protected promotion to exchange the passed pawn for the opposing bishop.
reviews.solutionVi: Đen đang bị chiếu. Nếu đi Kg5, Trắng chiếu hết bằng Rf5#. Đen đi Ke5 — Vua từ f6 đến e5, chấp nhận để Trắng bắt Tượng bằng Rxe7+. Sau Kxd5 Bc2, Đen đi Rh1 để bảo vệ ô phong cấp d1. Trắng chiếu Bb3+, Đen đáp Kc5. Sau Re2, Đen phong Hậu bằng d1=Q. Ván đấu tiếp diễn Bxd1 Rxd1. Đen đã đổi Tốt lấy Tượng trắng, bù lại Tượng đã mất.
hintsVi: Nếu Vua đen sang g5, Xe trắng có thể chiếu hết từ ô nào?
Tượng trắng ở c2 khống chế d1. Xe đen có thể đến đâu để bắt lại nếu Tượng bắt quân vừa phong?

reviewNotes.motifNecessity: White's Rf7+ checks the black king on f6, which currently guards the bishop e7. The only other legal move Kg5 allows Rf5#. Ke5 accepts Rxe7+ and leaves a concrete counterplay resource in the passed pawn d2. After Kxd5 Bc2 the rook must support the promotion square. Rh1 lets Black exchange the promotion piece for White's bishop.
reviewNotes.simplerAlternatives: Independently replayed all 48 legal solver roots across the five sample steps. After Rxe7+, Kd4 is a sound alternative and its reviewed Bc2 Rh1 Kf2 Rc1 Ba4 d1=Q still needs five solver moves. After Bc2, the strongest other rook moves materially underperform Rh1. White's equally strong Re2 immediately after Rh1 allows promotion on Black's fourth move. The sample Bb3+ is also comparably strong and adds a real king evasion, not a waiting move. At the fifth step the promotion to a rook and bishop, along with Rb1 and Rg1+, are viable in the bounds. The played queen promotion is an example.
reviewNotes.defencesAndRecovery: Independently replayed all 126 legal opponent replies across the five sample steps. Rxe7+ is the strongest acceptance, with the quiet decline Bc2 also reviewed. Bf7+ after Kxd5 is comparable to Bc2 and leads to a different rook placement and promotion. The strongest final reply Bxd1 permits an immediate, routine Rxd1, as played, leaving a stable one-rook ending. An added full-history 500k-node all-root check after Bxd1 found Rxd1 -5 nominal cp and Rg1+ -13 with later Rxd1; all other responses materially underperform. After Rh1 Re2, an added 500k all-root check independently confirms d1=Q or d1=R with Bxd1 Rxd1 as the same four-move solution mechanism.
reviewNotes.level: Four or five connected solver decisions depending on the strong reply. The bishop sacrifice is accepted, Rh1 is an essential promotion preparation, Bb3+ adds a real check in the played line, and the fifth move secures material recovery by immediate recapture.
reviewNotes.provenance: Replayed all 135 plies of Nikolic–Wohl, Parkroyal 2000, from PGN Mentor. White played 48.Rf7+, Black played 48...Ke5, and the full sample through 52...d1=Q is played, including its subsequent 53.Bxd1 Rxd1.
